scenario: [LINT.2.2]: an interval's element type is one `<` orders ([LINT.1.1]), and `Bool` is not one, so `b.flag .. b.other` on two `Bool` slots is refused with DS_VALIDATE_UNORDERED_TYPE. Both endpoints have one type, so the refusal cannot be LINT.2.2's mixed-family check (DS_VALIDATE_INTERVAL_MIXED_OPERANDS). A compiler that refuses only that compiles `true .. false`. The interval stands under `in` so the program is otherwise well formed. PATH PINNED: `dsc.typecheck`'s `lint_2_2_interval`, which refuses an unordered operand before it compares the two families.
rules_ds:
schema B scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    flag: Bool mutable
    other: Bool mutable

rule r:
    B b where b.flag in (b.flag .. b.other)
->
    log info "x"
